results.title: IHSG drops over 1% as PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) drags the index
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 84.62 points, or 1.33%, to 6,300.11 on 22 September 2026, extending the decline from the previous session. The drop was led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), which alone pulled the index down 14.6 points, followed by PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) (-7.74 points), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) (-2.98 points), PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) (-2.77 points), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) (-2.45 points), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (-2.21 points), PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) (-2.21 points), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) (-2.15 points), PT Impack Pratama Industri Tbk (IMPC) (-2.11 points) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) (-1.98 points). In contrast, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) added the most positive impact with +2.11 points, while PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) contributed +0.38 and +0.36 points respectively. Broad sector weakness saw energy, utilities and property lead the red zone, and the market remained sensitive to domestic uncertainty over the upcoming Bank Indonesia rate decision and global oil price and geopolitical tensions.

results.title: Stocks to Watch as the Fed Raises Interest Rates
results.body: Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia and RHB Sekuritas Indonesia recommend focusing on BBCA, BBRI, ELSA, MYOR, MDKA, MIKA, SMSM, LSIP and EXCL, citing consensus 12‑month target prices of Rp8,154, Rp3,851, Rp1,103, Rp2,483, Rp3,961, Rp2,715, Rp2,250, Rp1,933 and Rp3,267 respectively as of 21 September 2026, and noting that a majority of analysts rate BBCA and BBRI as buys. These recommendations follow the Federal Reserve’s 25‑basis‑point rate hike to a 3.75‑4 % target range last week, which is expected to tighten global monetary policy and increase funding costs for Indonesian equities.

results.title: Foreign investors net sold Rp 510.07 bn of Indonesian stocks, led by PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI)
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 510.07 bn on Monday, sending the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) down 0.88% to 6,384.72 points. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net outflows were PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) (Rp 140.61 bn), PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) (Rp 139.93 bn), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (Rp 131.34 bn), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) (Rp 114.62 bn), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) (Rp 32.42 bn), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) (Rp 26.38 bn), PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) (Rp 25.81 bn), PT Alamtri Resoruces Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) (Rp 22.32 bn), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) (Rp 21.98 bn), and PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk (ENRG) (Rp 16.65 bn). Overall market activity was high, with 26.78 billion shares traded for a total value of Rp 11.77 trillion. Sectorally, infrastructure fell 1.38% while transport rose 0.55%, health gained 0.21% and property remained flat.

results.title: Big bank stocks collectively weaken early in the week as investors adopt a wait-and-see stance ahead of the Bank Indonesia Governor Board meeting.
results.body: The article reports that on Monday 21 September 2026 the stocks of Indonesia’s four big banks – PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) and PT Bank Rakyaat Indonesia (BBRI) – all moved lower as investors adopted a wait-and-see stance ahead of the Bank Indonesia Governor Board meeting on 22-23 September. BMRI fell 1.53% to IDR 6,425 (opened at IDR 6,525) and has slipped 2.07% week-on-week, BBCA dropped 1.19% to IDR 6,225 (opened at IDR 6,300) after a 4.23% weekly decline, BBNI lost 0.82% to IDR 3,620 (opened at IDR 3,660) and is down 6.46% over the past week, while BBRI slipped 0.30% to IDR 3,300 (opened at IDR 3,310) after a 2.94% weekly fall. Analysts attribute the synchronized weakness to risk-off sentiment driven by a rupiah near IDR 17,700 per USD, 10-year US Treasury yields around 5%, and uncertainty over global interest-rate direction, while the market expects BI to keep the BI-Rate at 5.75% and the government’s extension of IDR 200 trillion of fund placements in state-owned banks through July 2027 may support liquidity. Despite the pull-back, BCA Sekuritas' Achmad Yaki recommends buying BBNI (target IDR 5,690) and BMRI (target IDR 6,500) and holding BBRI (target IDR 4,400), while Mirae Asset's Nafan Aji Gusta adds buy-add targets of IDR 7,900 for BBCA, IDR 4,020 for BBNI, IDR 4,720 for BMRI and IDR 3,570 for BBRI.

results.title: IHSG down 0.27% as foreign investors sell shares, with PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) among the most traded stocks
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 0.27% to 6,423.51 points in the first session on Monday 21 September, as foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp216.24 billion. Total transaction value on the exchange was Rp5.74 trillion with a volume of 14.28 billion shares, while 329 stocks rose, 291 fell and 168 were unchanged; six of eleven sector indices weakened, led by infrastructure down 0.40% and transport and logistics up 1.47%. PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) posted the highest transaction values at Rp233.97 billion and Rp225.99 billion respectively, with ANTM’s price slipping 1.50% and TPIA’s climbing 3.27%. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) were among the top net foreign sell stocks, with outflows of Rp19.05 billion and Rp50.77 billion respectively.

results.title: Analysts forecast IHSG weakness on Monday 21 Sep 2026 and recommend buying PT Buana Listya Tama Tbk (BULL), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (KLBF), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA).
results.body: Analysts note that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.53% to 6,441,159 last week, reflecting pressure from higher U.S. interest‑rate expectations. BEI’s market capitalization declined 1.58% to Rp11,266 trillion, while average daily transaction value dropped 6.95% to Rp15.22 trillion and average daily volume fell 20.71% to 28.61 billion shares. MNC Sekuritas recommends investors consider a buy‑on‑weakness position in PT Buana Listya Tama Tbk (BULL), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (KLBF) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM). It also advises a buying trade for PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) as the index remains above the 6,370 support level, offering upside toward 6,541‑6,581.

results.title: Caution Over Fed Sentiment as Indonesia’s Composite Index May Test 6,290 Next Week
results.body: The article warns that hawkish Fed sentiment could push the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) to test the 6,290‑6,370 range next week. MNC Sekuritas places the index in wave iv of wave (c) on the black label, with support at 6,279 and 6,201 and resistance at 6,585 and 6,633, and notes that staying above 6,370 could allow a rise to 6,541‑6,581. IHSG fell 1.53% to 6,441,159 on Friday, with market capitalization down 1.58% to Rp11,266 trillion, average daily transaction value down 6.95% to Rp15.22 trillion, and foreign investors net‑selling Rp1.79 trillion (cumulative Rp74.36 trillion in 2026). MNC Sekuritas recommends buying on weakness PT Buana Listya Tama Tbk (BULL), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (KLBF) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM), and a buy for PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA).

results.title: Foreign investors sell shares of major banks and Prajogo‑linked stocks
results.body: Foreign investors net sold shares of major banks and Prajogo‑linked stocks during the week of 14–18 September 2026. The largest net sell was PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp798 billion, followed by PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) with Rp443.2 billion, PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) with Rp193.2 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) with Rp189.9 billion, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) with Rp166.3 billion, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) with Rp132.6 billion, PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) with Rp95 billion, PT Timah Tbk (TINS) with Rp47.7 billion, PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) with Rp45 billion and PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) with Rp44.6 billion. Foreign investors’ net sell for the week totaled Rp1.84 trillion, contributing to a 1.53% decline in the IHSG to 6,441,159 and a 1.58% drop in market capitalization to Rp11,266 trillion, while average daily transaction value, frequency and volume fell 6.95%, 14.73% and 20.71% respectively. The sell‑off coincided with the Federal Reserve’s 25‑basis‑point rate hike to a target range of 3.75‑4% on 16 September 2026 and analysts’ view that further US rate increases may prompt Bank Indonesia to consider similar moves.

results.title: Foreign outflow hits Rp1.79 trillion, with BBCA and BMRI leading net sells
results.body: On 18 September 2024, foreign investors recorded a net outflow of Rp1.78 trillion on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, with foreign buying rising to Rp7.04 trillion and selling to Rp8.81 trillion. The largest net‑sell positions were posted by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) with Rp222.05 billion (35.43 million shares) and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) with Rp108.93 billion (25.45 million shares), followed by PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI). The top net‑buy positions were held by PT Aneka Tambang (Persero) Tbk (ANTM) at Rp41.09 billion (12.49 million shares), PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) at Rp22.40 billion (4.55 million shares), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) at Rp15.59 billion (1.27 million shares), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) at Rp12.47 billion (4.28 million shares) and PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) at Rp10.48 billion (19.88 million shares). These figures show the breadth of foreign trading activity across major banks, telecom, mining and battery‑materials stocks.

results.title: Grup Djarum, Low Tuck Kwong, and Prajogo Pangestu Stocks Weigh Down the IHSG for the Week
results.body: During the week of 7–11 September 2026, shares of PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bayan Resources Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk, PT Barito Pacific Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk, and PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk fell sharply, delivering the largest negative contributions to the IHSG, with BBCA down 5.60% (‑33.09 points), BYAN down 10.51% (‑23.63 points), BBRI down 3.54% (‑17.51 points), DSSA down 6.78% (‑6.86 points), BBNI down 4.82% (‑6.26 points), BRMS down 5.59% (‑5.95 points), BRPT down 5.03% (‑5.22 points), BMRI down 1.36% (‑4.90 points), BREN down 3.57% (‑4.64 points), and VKTR down 8.09% (‑4.31 points). The composite index slipped 1.43% to 6,541,377, while total market capitalization fell 1.32% to Rp11,446 trillion and average daily transaction value dropped 14.88% to Rp16.36 trillion. Foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp690.19 billion on 11 September, contributing to a year‑to‑date net outflow of Rp71,415 trillion.

results.title: Mirae Asset Sekuritas assesses global pressures still weighing on the market
results.body: Mirae Asset Sekuritas says global sentiment continues to weigh on Indonesia’s market, noting that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.33% to 6,589 amid a net foreign outflow of Rp748 billion. The pressure was most evident on banking stocks BBCA and BBRI, while foreign investors accumulated commodity‑linked shares such as ANTM, AADI, CUAN and PTBA. The firm cites macro factors including the US 10‑year Treasury yield near 5%, the ECB rate at 2.5%, high oil prices, the rupiah at roughly Rp17,547 per USD and a 10‑year SBN yield of 7.11% as limiting the transmission of global yields to the domestic market. Despite these headwinds, consumer confidence rose to 118.5 in August and Mirae Asset recommends a selective portfolio focused on strong fundamentals and solid cash flow.

results.title: IHSG Falls 1.49% in First Session as Global Markets Slide on Oil Surge and Fed Rate Hike Bets
results.body: The Indonesian Composite Stock Price Index (IHSG) fell 1.49% to 6,490 in the first trading session on Friday, driven by heavy selling pressure across the market. Big-cap stocks BYAN, BBCA, and BRMS were the primary weights on the index, while transport, non-primary consumer, and infrastructure sectors led declines of more than 1.7% each. The selloff tracked a broad decline across Asian markets as Brent crude surged above $108 per barrel and stronger-than-expected US producer inflation increased the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike to 70%. The rupiah weakened to 17,610 per US dollar amid dollar strength fueled by rate hike expectations. Panin Sekuritas cited escalating geopolitical tensions, oil above $100 per barrel, and heavy foreign outflows as key drivers.

results.title: Indonesian rupiah and IHSG pressured by surge in oil prices amid US-Iran tensions.
results.body: The Indonesian stock market (IHSG) fell 1.33% to 6,589.34 and the rupiah weakened 0.2% to 17,547 per US dollar on Thursday, pressured by a surge in Brent crude oil prices above $100 per barrel amid escalating US-Iran tensions. The decline marked the IHSG's lowest level in a week and made it the worst-performing emerging market index in Asia Pacific, with all sectoral indices down, led by energy (-2.06%) and transportation (-1.80%). Trading value reached Rp21.58 trillion with 51 billion shares exchanged, with PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk among the most actively traded stocks. Most Asian emerging market currencies weakened against the dollar, though the Malaysian ringgit and Chinese yuan edged higher.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk announces quarterly interim dividend plan for 2026
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk announced that it will pay interim dividends on a quarterly basis in 2026. The next interim dividend of Rp25 per share is scheduled for 16 September 2026, up from Rp20 per share paid in June 2026, with a further interim dividend planned for December 2026. The company reported a dividend payout ratio of 72% for the most recent period, up from 68%, and total profit of Rp29.5 trillion for the first half of 2026, including its subsidiaries. Credit grew 8% year‑on‑year to Rp1,036 trillion and CASA rose 10.2% year‑on‑year to Rp1,082 trillion, supporting the dividend policy.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk Reports Credit Growth to Rp1,036 Trillion and NPL Decline to 1.9% in First Half 2026
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BCA) disclosed in its 2026 public expose that credit expanded 8% year-on-year to Rp1,036 trillion as of June 2026, driven by productive credit growth of 11% to Rp802 trillion and corporate lending growth of 13.6% to Rp513.4 trillion. Asset quality improved with the non-performing loan ratio falling to 1.9% from 2.2% a year earlier and the loan-at-risk ratio easing to 4.9% from 5.7%. Third-party funds rose 7.9% to Rp1,284 trillion, supported by a current account savings account (CASA) ratio of 85.2%. The bank and its subsidiaries recorded a net profit of Rp29.5 trillion for the first half of 2026, while green financing grew 19% to Rp123 trillion. Meanwhile, BBCA shares have declined 18.69% year-to-date to Rp6,525.

results.title: BCA Announces Up to Rp5 Trillion Share Buyback Program Running Until March 2027
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk has an ongoing share buyback program of up to Rp5 trillion that runs until March 2027. The company has already repurchased approximately Rp3.5 trillion of shares since last year. The program was approved at the 2026 annual general meeting and covers a 12-month period from March 2026 to March 2027. Management says buybacks will be executed when market conditions are overly volatile to demonstrate confidence in the bank's fundamentals.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk to pay interim dividend of Rp25 per share on 16 September 2026
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk announced an interim dividend of Rp25 per share payable on 16 September 2026. The payout is part of a new quarterly dividend policy that will see dividends distributed in June, September, December and a final dividend in March 2027 after the shareholders' meeting. The interim amount is higher than the Rp20 per share paid in June 2026. Under the quarterly schedule, shareholders can expect dividend payments each quarter throughout the 2026 fiscal year.

results.title: IHSG falls 0.58% in first session as foreign investors net sell Rp577 billion, led by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) declined 0.58% to 6,647.50 in the first trading session on Wednesday (9/9), with total transaction value reaching Rp8.32 trillion. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp577.21 billion, dominated by bank stocks with the largest market capitalization. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk posted the largest net foreign sell of Rp419.03 billion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk at Rp62.73 billion. Most sectoral indices weakened, with healthcare down 1.45% and technology down 1%, while transportation gained 2.15%. Regional Asian markets were mixed, with South Korea's KOSPI rising 1.01% and India's NIFTY falling 0.52%.

results.title: Foreign investors net buy hundreds of billions of rupiah in a day, snapping up ten stocks
results.body: On Tuesday, 8 September 2026, foreign investors recorded a net purchase of Rp398.12 billion across the Indonesian stock market. In the regular market segment, net buying reached Rp379.39 billion, with the largest single‑stock net buy of Rp269.68 billion in PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, whose shares rose 0.75% to Rp6,675. PT Bumi Resources Tbk experienced the biggest net sell of Rp178.07 billion, yet its stock gained 2.73% to close at Rp226. The broader market reflected the buying trend, as the Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) closed in the green zone at 6,686 points, up 66.77 points (1.01%).

results.title: IHSG forecast to reach 6,700 amid Anak Krakatau eruption concerns, with BBCA, BBRI, BMRI under pressure and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommending IMPC, TINS, KOTA, UDNG.
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) could climb to the 6,600‑6,700 range, with a key resistance at 6,700, despite the ongoing Anak Krakatau eruption. On Monday the index slipped 0.25% to 6,619.67, staying above the 20‑day moving average and with a positive MACD, while foreign‑exchange reserves rose to US$146.5 billion supporting domestic sentiment. Technical pressure is coming from BBCA, BBRI and BMRI, whereas BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends swing‑trade positions in IMPC and TINS, a day‑trade in KOTA, and a sell stance on UDNG. The market’s near‑term direction may be swayed by the U.S. CPI release on 11 September, projected at 3.4% headline and 2.4% core inflation, which could affect risk appetite and the index’s trajectory.
